## Linear description

Parent: WIL-3245. Design: [https://willayam.github.io/clarity-design-previews/agent-access-build-design/](<https://willayam.github.io/clarity-design-previews/agent-access-build-design/>) (§9 row 2, §10 "Agent 2"). Follows Agent access 1 (WIL-3543, merged as #1012) and the WorkOS spike Part A, which passed on 2026-10-05.

**Why.** Every agent write needs a record, a replay rule and a revocation rule before the first write ships. Agents also need to read the Library, videos, pages and stats.

**Scope.**

* Migration `0042_agent_access.sql`, the next free number: `agent_connections`, `agent_actions` and `agent_approvals`, plus a `jobs` index for the later daily cap. Row types regenerated.
* Connections:
  * one row per WorkOS user and OAuth client;
  * `client_id` required on every token, as the spike observed on all hosts;
  * a revoked connection stays refused even with a refreshed token;
  * after any revoke, a new client lands `pending` until the owner enables it, because ChatGPT and Codex mint per-install client ids;
  * at most ten connections per user.
* One policy dispatcher:
  * permission check, then a rate limit per connection;
  * entitlement for writes through the wall's own function, with a 5-minute walled cache and a 503 on a Stripe or D1 error;
  * replay scoped to operation and target, matching only successful rows, with server-minted ids;
  * an audit row for every write;
  * a 90-day sweep on the cron.
* Read operations:
  * `library_list`, `videos_get` (waits up to 45 s, asking Mux on the first and last poll only), `pages_get` (document marked untrusted) and `pages_stats`;
  * `pages_leads` and `contacts_list`, both behind a per-connection leads permission that starts off, with prospect text marked untrusted;
  * `approvals_get`;
  * `whoami` gains the connection.
* Owner API with the session cookie: list connections, revoke, enable, toggle the leads permission. Impersonated sessions are refused on every write.

**Acceptance.**

* The policy matrix passes on the real SQL fake.
* A revoked connection refuses a refreshed token.
* An unseen client after a revoke lands pending, and an eleventh connection is refused.
* Replay never collides across targets and never blocks a retry after a failure.
* `pages_leads` refuses until the owner turns the permission on.
* No entitlement SQL under `agent/`.
* An impersonated session is refused on every write.

**Verify on the PR preview.** `scripts/agent-mcp.mjs conformance` lists the read operations and the seeded account's Library. Revoke, pending and enable work through the API.

**Size.** 5 pipeline days. **Blocked by.** WIL-3543 (done). **Merge routing: steer** (auth policy change). Before merge, list pending production migrations: this PR adds one, and a stack deploy applies the whole backlog.

### williamlarsten@​gmail.com on 2026-10-06T00:14:26.914Z
Source comment: https://linear.app/cocco/issue/WIL-3544/agent-access-2-connections-audit-policy-dispatcher-read-operations#comment-7e80db66

> *This was generated by AI during implementation.*

## Proof

**PR:** https://github.com/Clarity-Video-HQ/clarity/pull/1024 at head `fceecd7f3`. **Routing:** steer (auth policy change).
**Preview:** https://pr-1024.clarity-video.workers.dev, which serves `fceecd7f33f83fe8b8ef847ebf90850d43c8147c`.

**Verdict: VERIFIED.** An independent Fable verifier wrote none of the code and none of the first evidence. It ran every check below on the preview's own database.

| Acceptance | Evidence on the preview |
|---|---|
| A new client gets an active connection | `whoami` 200, `connection` active; the same id appears in the owner list and in D1 |
| A revoked connection refuses a refreshed token | revoke, mint a new token: `initialize` is HTTP 403 `connection_revoked` with the Settings URL; enable, and the same token works |
| After any revoke, an unseen client lands pending | a new client answers 403 `connection_pending` and shows `pending` in the list until enabled; then `whoami` is 200 |
| Ten live connections at most | the eleventh unseen client is 403 `too_many_connections`; revoking one frees a slot; re-enabling a revoked one while ten are live answers 409 |
| Leads permission starts off | `pages_leads` and `contacts_list` refuse with `permission_required` until `PATCH {leadsContacts:true}`, then answer |
| Reads are projected and untrusted text is marked | `library_list` items carry only `id,type,title,updatedAt,folderId`; `pages_get` wraps the document as untrusted; unknown ids answer `not_found` |
| The owner API is owner-only | no cookie is 401; a foreign Origin is 403; another user's connection id is 404 for revoke, enable and PATCH |
| Migration 0042 | the three tables and their indexes exist on the preview database; `agent_actions` holds 0 rows after about 40 reads (reads are not audited) |
| Adjacent flow | a userPro sign-in and `control-clarity doctor --pr 1024` are green |

The extended `scripts/agent-mcp.mjs conformance` on the preview passed 13/13: both metadata paths, 401 with `resource_metadata`, cookie refusal, the eight read tools all read-only, `whoami` with its connection, and the `pages_leads` refusal.

**Review.** Three rounds, one Fable reviewer and one GPT-6 Astra cross-family seat.
- Astra's blocker was fixed: "pending after any revoke" now keys on `revoked_at` history.
- Also fixed:
  - connection admission is one guarded statement, so it can't race past the cap;
  - re-enabling a revoked connection respects the live cap;
  - a Stripe outage answers 503 and is never cached as walled, while a Stripe 4xx is treated as an answer;
  - an audit-insert failure surfaces instead of vanishing.
- The final round is clean.

**Not covered by the preview run.** The write-path machinery (replay, audit rows, idempotency conflict, Stripe 503, impersonated sessions refused, the sweep) is pinned by unit tests, because PR 2 ships no write operation. `videos_get` on a real video was not exercised: the preview account has no video.


</details>
